Observed facts: during elective open inguinal hernia repair two separate spermatic‑cord bundles were encountered. Each bundle contained a vas deferens together with arterial, venous and neural elements, and both were followed distally to the testis and proximally through a single internal inguinal ring. No prior inguinal surgery, trauma, urinary or testicular symptoms were reported and the scrotal examination was normal. No preoperative imaging had been performed.

Hypotheses: the finding most likely represents a duplicated spermatic cord or a bifid cord variant rather than a true second testis, because both structures converge at a common internal ring and each carries a vas. An alternative is an accessory vascular bundle accompanying a single cord, but the presence of two distinct vasa makes duplication more plausible.

Immediate safety and documentation priorities: preserve both vasa, vessels and nerves; avoid ligation or division of either bundle. Record the anatomy with intra‑operative photographs and a detailed operative note describing the number, course and relationships of the structures. Communicate the finding to the pathology and radiology teams for correlation.

Proposed further confirmation: obtain a postoperative scrotal ultrasound (or MRI if indicated) to verify testicular number, vascular supply and vas continuity. This imaging is for documentation and future counseling, not because the variant should have been predicted preoperatively.
